name: Dialogue Portraits (Gen 3)
description: FireRed/LeafGreen port of the Dialogue Portraits mod: shows a portrait of whoever is talking, next to the dialogue box. INSET puts the art inside the box in four of its own columns -- a 32-pixel portrait filling its slot edge to edge, with one more column kept clear of the words -- so the text gets the same 21 columns on either side; FRAMED gives it the game's own standard menu window -- the same Chrome.stdFrame the start menu's box and the OPTION page's body are drawn with, so it is drawn in the player's own OPTION -> FRAME choice and wears the real extracted tiles -- six tiles (48 pixels) square, with a whole tile (8 pixels) of border on every side around a 32-pixel content rect; the border is drawn from 8x8 tiles and only lines up on the tile grid, so the window is ONE size for everybody and the ART is the thing that varies, fitted into the content at the largest whole number of times its own crop that fits -- the default 32-pixel face at 1:1 filling the content exactly, a 16-pixel crop at 2x also filling it, a 12-pixel one at 2x with four pixels of content either side -- and never resampled to an arbitrary fit; the window is a constant, so the text width is a constant again -- 152 pixels for every speaker in this layout, which reverses 1.8.0's per-speaker width -- and the run the box gives up is a constant seven columns; the panel is centred in that run, keeping 4 pixels from the play area's own edge and the same 4 from the box's visible edge, so the distance from the portrait to the nearest letter is that 4 plus the box's own 16-pixel border -- 20 pixels, on both sides -- and the portrait touches neither the box nor the screen, and on a phone it no longer runs off the side of the device; MARGIN paints a panel of its own out in the letterbox, or above the box when there is no letterbox to use -- keeping 2 game pixels clear of the box's top and 4 in from the edge of the play area, so it touches neither the box nor the screen's edge -- and leaves the box alone at 26 -- and because it costs the text nothing it draws the same window FRAMED does -- the game's own 48-pixel menu frame around a content rect the art is centred in at a whole-number zoom -- so a small crop is enlarged by a whole number rather than stretched to fill the window, and the panel is 48 pixels rather than the 32 that 1.8.0 gave it, which is what the letterbox condition is measured against. The panel is placed in the window's own units, measured against the rect the frame was actually drawn at -- asked of the renderer through require, not package.loaded, because a mod's sandbox hands it a decoy package whose loaded is empty -- rather than the one the engine reports -- the reported rect comes from Display.fit (48% of the safe area, scale from the width alone) while the frame is drawn from the touch skin's own cutout (a fraction of the window, scale from both axes), and the two agree only when no skin is selected, which is why a desktop never showed it and a phone showed up to 41 game pixels of error; a panel placed against the reported box sat anywhere from 33 game pixels inside the real box to 46 above it -- and in units derived from the playfield rectangle when there is no renderer to ask, because scale is integer framebuffer pixels per game pixel while the playfield is in window units and the two differ by the display's pixel ratio, which is 1 on a desktop and 2 or 3 on a phone. So it sits the same distance above the box at any pixel density instead of drifting off the bottom of the frame on a high-DPI screen, and that clearance is stated in game pixels so it is the same margin on every device rather than a different one per screen. Every layout also tells the engine's word-wrap its own text width, so lines break where they are drawn rather than being clipped at the tail; and where narrowing the wrap would leave a page holding a single word, the last word of the line above moves down to join it, so no box asks for a button press to read one word. SIDE = AUTO puts the face on whichever side of the screen the player turned towards. Ships no ROM art: every portrait is cut at runtime out of the battle art the engine extracted from your own ROM -- a trainer class frontpic or a species frontpic, at the path the extracted data itself gives -- using a per-character rectangle from art/crops.lua -- keyed by the front picture, by the species key the engine's own keyName fold gives for a Pokemon, or, where two speakers share a picture and are not framed the same way, by the person through a name:, gfx:, sprite: or class: prefix -- and drawn through the game's own palette so it sits in the frame like part of the game. The cart's own graphics id the object carries is consulted before the class, because the host's sprite vocabulary collapses several people onto one sprite and drops every graphic its table does not list onto a Youngster's: a graphic is one person or one uniform while a class can cover eight gym leaders, so it is what says a Hiker is not a PokeFan and which of the eight leaders sharing one class is standing in the room, and it answers with an exact front picture, or with a name, or -- where the cart never drew the person a battle bust -- with no portrait at all. It also answers where the host's vocabulary names the WRONG person rather than nobody: a Camper and a Picnicker are mapped onto the Youngster and the Lass sprites, and a male and a female Cooltrainer or Tuber share one sprite, so those graphics resolve to their own kind and their own sex by their own picture instead of through the class name -- and a Man and a Balding Man, who share the Hiker's sprite and were wearing a boy's face, decline the way the Fat Man does. A trainer's own face is found from the SCRIPT the object runs, not from its sprite: the map event does not carry the trainer class -- the extractor keeps the object's scriptKey and drops trainerType, so that field is 0 for every NPC including the trainers -- and the mod brings its own table instead, art/trainer_ids.lua, which maps a script's own key to the cart's numeric trainer id, dug out of the trainerbattle opcode at the head of that script for all 432 trainer objects in the cart; that id is translated to the trainer's own front picture through the engine's own trainer pack, which is the only route that can tell the eight Super Nerds from the fourteen Scientists who share one overworld sprite, and it is consulted before the graphics table and before the class, so it also answers where the graphics table deliberately declines; where the object's class IS known -- a trainer who challenges you, whose battle payload carries it -- the class is translated to the picture through the pack as before, and FireRed keeps the class and the picture in two different number spaces, so the class is never used as a picture id; the character's name is a second, exact route; an ordinary NPC, which carries no class at all (objects.lua sets trainerType 0 for every object that is not a battle object), is named by its own SPRITE_* id and resolved to the class whose battle art is the same kind of person; a talking Pokemon from the object's own SPRITE_* id, resolved through the dex. A named speaker is read from the dialogue's own "NAME: " prefix. The rival is the one speaker the cart never spells out -- his dialogue carries the FD 06 placeholder where the name belongs and the engine expands it to whatever the player typed, so he is recognised by the name on the save and resolved through his own picture rather than by the text. A PNG dropped in CustomArt/ always wins. A portrait is only ever drawn for a dialogue that belongs to somebody: the engine's own world.talk seam -- raised for every A press that reaches an object with a script -- is what names a speaker, so signs, hidden items, field moves and every menu box come out bare; the box's own frame kind is checked as well, so a box the engine opens for a battle, an evolution or an egg hatch stays bare too, even with a conversation still on record. A trainer who challenges you has no A press behind their box: a line-of-sight trainer sees the player and the engine starts their script from a step, which raises no world.talk, so the engine's own world.trainer_engaged event -- emitted from that same function with the trainer's own object -- is what names the speaker there. Its two settings, PORTRAIT and SIDE, live in a DIALOGUE PORTRAITS group inside FireRed's own OPTION menu, drawn by FireRed's own chrome and font -- Gen 3 has no route to the engine's mod manager, and the mod does not push a foreign menu. Gen 3-only: it does not load on Red, Blue, Yellow, Gold, Silver or Crystal -- use gen1recomp-dialogue-portraits or gen2-dialogue-portraits there. 1.9.2 answers two more of the host's own vocabularies that were naming the wrong person. FRLG lists its Hoenn trainer classes first and repeats 31 of those names for its own Kanto classes further down -- LASS is 49 and again 59 -- so a class name is now resolved to the class the cart actually fields trainers under rather than to the lowest id, which is what put the Hoenn Lass on the girl on Route 3 and the Hoenn Fisherman, Beauty, Sailor, Black Belt and Gentleman on every pier, towel and deck in Kanto. And FRLG's Pokemon graphics ids -- 109 SNORLAX through 150 DEOXYS_N, all of them above the 92 the host sprite table stops at -- now name their species outright, so the Spearow in the Viridian house and every other Pokemon standing in the world gets its own portrait where it had none at all. 1.9.3 is the same two questions asked of everything else. The wrong faces -- a Super Nerd wearing the Scientist's picture, twins wearing the Lass's, the old bald man in the blue robe wearing the old karate instructor's -- were all one defect, a trainer's class guessed from a shared overworld sprite; they are answered from the script now, as above, which is the only route that can tell the eight Super Nerds from the fourteen Scientists. And the framing was re-measured portrait by portrait rather than trusting one general crop: seven Pokemon and one trainer picture were framed on the wrong part of their art, and four of them -- Fearow, Pidgeot, Zapdos and Moltres -- had a WING in the frame and no face at all, because the species rule centres a creature's own box and a bird drawn with its wings spread is mostly wing; each now has a rectangle centred on its face, measured by rendering the window over the whole sprite and looking at the result. 1.9.4 answers the question that sentence left open: how the game itself decides which portrait belongs to a trainer. The answer is that the overworld sprite never decides it -- a sprite is a uniform, and uniforms are shared. OBJ_EVENT_GFX_ROCKER, the yellow-haired figure, is worn by 28 trainer objects: 18 Bird Keepers, 9 Jugglers and exactly one Rocker. Sixteen of the 34 graphics a trainer can wear are shared that way by two or more classes whose pictures differ, so no value per sprite can be right for them and the trainer's own id is the only fact that can be. So the rule is two rules. A TRAINER gets his own picture, by id, through the script route 1.9.3 added -- all 432 trainer objects in the game resolve to the id's own front pic, and 0 of them do not. A NON-TRAINER has no trainer data at all, so his sprite is the only fact about him and he gets one consistent picture per graphic. The reported cases: the Fuchsia City fat man's box opens "ERIK: Where's SARA?" and ERIK is a real Super Nerd whose picture 89 is the lab coat that was reported as a Scientist's -- he is not that fat man, and the fat man's own graphic is one the cart drew no bust of, so the text-name route no longer gets to overrule a graphic that has already declined; the Bird Keeper is picture 104 and not the Rocker's 101, because the yellow-haired art is 104's; Engineer Braxton's own answer was already right, but the graphic he wears answered nobody, so the 28 non-trainers sharing his sprite had no face at all -- gfx 30 is the cart's own overworld sprite for the Engineer and picture 93 is its bust; the red-haired little girl is one of the Twins, picture 127, and not a Lass. The couple is the one case where a single picture genuinely holds two people: pictures 127 through 131 draw two figures, so art/crops.lua now carries a pair of windows for each and a graphic-to-half table, and the object's own sprite picks the half it stands on -- the woman in a Young Couple wears gfx 29 and gets the left half, the man gfx 25 and the right, so JES and GIA no longer wear the same face. Sweeping every line of every object in the game for the ERIK shape -- a name in a box that belongs to somebody else -- found one more, Daisy Oak, who was wearing a Five Island Painter's face because the pack has a DAISY too; she declines now, while Lorelei and Selphy, who really are the trainers they name, keep theirs. And every window in the crop table -- 50 of them -- was re-measured on all four edges: two were wrong, the left Twin's head had two columns cut off its side and the right half of picture 130 had the top of a ponytail cut off, and both are fixed and pinned by number, because a window that fits inside the source can still be cutting the face inside it. 1.9.5 answers a report that named four portraits and, underneath, found the reason the 1.9.3 and 1.9.4 work was not visible in that boot. The rule the report asked for is a real one and is now in the mod: a graphic is a uniform and uniforms are shared, so the map decides which class is standing here. art/map_art.lua is generated by walking every map and recording, for each graphic, the picture its own trainers resolve to -- 91 maps, 228 graphic-to-picture pairs, 11 of them splits where one graphic is worn by two classes on one map and the majority wins. It is consulted BETWEEN the trainer's own id and the graphics table, and it has to be there rather than above the id, because the two disagree for 17 of the game's 432 trainer objects -- a Route 16 Biker standing among Hikers, a Kindle Road Cooltrainer among Black Belts -- and in every one of those the cart named that man himself, so his id is the fact to believe. So the yellow-haired graphic 26 is the Juggler in Fuchsia Gym, the Bird Keeper on Route 13 and the Rocker on Route 12, and graphic 55 is the Super Nerd on Route 8 and the Scientist in Silph Co. What the report actually caught, though, was the graphics table being reached at all: a Super Nerd wearing the Scientist's picture 107, a Juggler wearing the Bird Keeper's 104, and an Aroma Lady -- whose graphic had no value at all -- wearing nothing. Those are exactly the values the one-value-per-graphic table gives, which means the id route was not firing, and it was not firing because it depends on the cart's trainer table and that table is a GENERATED cache: on a boot without it every trainer falls past the id and lands on the graphic. Two things follow. The graphics table gained a default for the two shared sprites that needed one -- the Scientist for graphic 55 and the Aroma Lady for 28, the majority class of each -- so the fallback is at worst the most common wearer rather than a different class or nobody; and the location route answers the reported cases 8 of 8 through the real engine loader on a boot with no trainer table at all. Underneath both there was a second defect worth the words: the mod's own trainer index was being memoised BEFORE the engine was asked for the pack, so a first call that found nothing cached an empty index for the rest of the session and the id route stayed dead even after the table appeared. The empty index is no longer stored, so the next call retries. Measured honestly, the location route changes exactly one non-trainer in the whole game -- a Lady on Five Island standing among Ladies, 144 to 146 -- and 5 of its 6 answers already agree with what the mod said; it earns its place as the answer when the generated table is missing, not as a correction on a complete boot. And the Seel portrait was measured against the WRONG PICTURE: a species is shown its own front pic -- speciesArt hands record.index to Pokemon.frontPic -- and SEEL's internal species id is 86, not 87. Pokemon.frontPic(86) is byte-identical to .probe/_art/mon-86.png, proved by .probe/dp3_seel_engine.lua; mon-87 is Dewgong. Seel's face sits at the BOTTOM CENTRE of its sprite -- muzzle bbox (18,42)-(34,51), tongue (20,47)-(27,52) -- so both the rule's own answer {13,5,32} and the first cut of this entry {4,4,32} framed the top lobes and left the whole face outside. The window is now {12,21,32}.
